h1: Travelodge Pattaya — 3-Star Chain in Central Pattaya with a Rooftop Sky Pool, Walkable to the Beach
intro: If you want a chain hotel where you know exactly what you're getting for a few thousand baht, right in the middle of Central Pattaya where everything is within walking distance — Travelodge Pattaya, opened in 2014, is a name that comes up often · The 164-room building sits on Soi 15 next to The Avenue Pattaya mall, with a rooftop sky pool overlooking the city, a 24-hour gym, and The Lodge all-day dining restaurant · It's about a 1 km walk to Pattaya Beach and Walking Street · Prices start from around THB 1,000/night on weekdays · 8.8 from 436 Trip.com reviews and 8.3 from Booking.com

body.html: Travelodge Pattaya overview — who it's for — To put it as simply as possible, Travelodge Pattaya is a 3-star chain hotel for people who want a "no surprises" stay on an affordable budget, right in the middle of Central Pattaya where you can walk almost anywhere · It isn't a beachfront resort that lulls you to sleep with the sound of the waves, and it isn't a luxury 5-star place selling spa treatments and butlers · Instead it's a chain hotel that focuses on doing the basics well — clean rooms, comfortable beds, free Wi-Fi, a rooftop sky pool, and a location in the middle of everything · It has been open since 2014 under the Travelodge brand, which travelers worldwide recognize as an affordable hotel with a consistent standard · It's still open today and reviews very well, scoring 8.8 from 436 reviews on Trip.com and 8.3 on Booking.com · Real guest reviews agree that the people best suited to it are couples, solo travelers, groups of friends, and small families who want a spot within walking distance of the beach and the food-and-drink scene, rather than those after a spacious room or a full sea view · Another group that says it's impressed is first-time visitors to Pattaya who don't want to risk staying far from the city center, because once you're here you barely have to plan your transport — everything is within walking distance or a short songthaew ride · It's a hotel that plays the "good value and convenient" card to the hilt while still holding on to a standard of cleanliness and service you don't often find at this price.

Location and getting around — This is unquestionably Travelodge Pattaya's number-one selling point · The hotel sits on Soi 15 (Soi Pattaya 15) on the Nongprue, Bang Lamung side, right next to The Avenue Pattaya mall, which pulls together restaurants, a supermarket, a cinema, and shops in one place — just a few steps from the lobby · Within walking distance there's a 7-Eleven across the street, plus a Villa Market, street-food stalls, cafes, and massage shops everywhere · On distances: it's about a 1–1.4 km walk to Pattaya Beach and roughly 1 km to Walking Street (an easy 12–18 min walk, or a few baht by songthaew) · It's near popular landmarks like Ripley's Believe It or Not and Louis Tussaud's Waxworks, both within a 500 m radius · CentralFestival Pattaya Beach is about 2–2.5 km away, a few minutes by car · Importantly, it's about a 40 min drive from U-Tapao Airport (UTP) and roughly 2 hr from Bangkok, handy for anyone driving themselves or catching a van/bus from Ekkamai or Mo Chit · One small note: Soi 15 is in the middle of the nightlife district, so nights are fairly lively, and if you walk back late there are still plenty of people about.

"Great location — step out of the hotel and you're surrounded by 7-Elevens and restaurants, and it's an easy walk to the beach and Walking Street. For this price, having a rooftop pool to soak in come evening is better value than I expected."

Room types and decor — Travelodge Pattaya has 164 rooms in total, split into several types for different group sizes · It starts with Standard Plus (King bed) and Standard Twin (two single beds), compact entry rooms of about 20–22 sqm, good for a couple or two friends · Stepping up are Standard Queen and the family Friends and Family Quadruple, which has a King bed plus two sofa beds and sleeps up to 4, suited to families or groups of friends · The decor is clean and modern, in light tones, with the easy-to-use practicality you expect from a chain · Every room has air conditioning, a flat-screen TV, a fridge/minibar, a safe, blackout curtains, free drinking water, and a shower bathroom with basic amenities · Many reviews agree that the rooms are very clean, the beds are comfortable, and it's well maintained for a hotel that's no longer brand new · But to be straight with you, the point that comes up most often is the fairly small room size and the lack of a balcony — the bathroom and shower space are compact to match · This is normal for a chain hotel in the middle of a city designed to make the most of its footprint; anyone who wants room to spread out their luggage or spends a lot of time in the room might want to move up to a Queen or family room, which are a bit larger · For those who use the hotel as just a place to sleep before heading out all day, the entry room size is plenty comfortable.

Facilities, pool and gym — The most talked-about highlight at Travelodge Pattaya is the rooftop sky pool that looks out over the Pattaya cityscape as a backdrop · Late afternoon into the evening is the popular time for guests to head up to chill, take photos, and sip a drink at the poolside bar · There are sunbathing spots and loungers to relax on, and plenty of kids take a particular liking to this pool · On the fitness side there's a 24-hour gym for anyone who wants to work out after a day of sightseeing or before starting a new one · There's also a lobby, cafe, bar, luggage storage, a counter that helps with tour bookings and arranging cars, and free Wi-Fi throughout · To be honest, the rooftop pool isn't a resort-style lap pool — several reviews say it's fairly small but enough for a cooling-off dip and some photos of the view · In terms of atmosphere and getting a rooftop pool at this price, it's well done for a mid-city chain hotel, and it's the thing that makes Travelodge feel like better value than similarly priced hotels without a pool.

Food and bar — The hotel's main restaurant is The Lodge, which serves all-day dining covering Western, Asian, Italian, and Thai dishes · In the morning there's a Western-Asian breakfast buffet (around 6:00 AM–10:30 AM) that many reviews praise as varied and filling for a hotel of this level · One thing to know is that some room packages don't include breakfast and you pay extra per person (children up to 17 usually go free), so check when booking whether the package you pick includes it or not · For other meals, the hotel's location helps a lot, because just step out the door and you'll find restaurants, street food, and the shops in the adjacent Avenue mall — so many people choose to eat out rather than dine in the hotel every meal, which is part of the appeal of staying in Central Pattaya · The rooftop poolside bar is another spot to sip an evening drink with a nice atmosphere and a city view at the same time · Overall, food isn't the reason to come to Travelodge for in-hotel dining; it's a decent, convenient add-on that fits the style of using the hotel as a base to explore the city.

Service — Service is another point that earns consistent praise in real reviews · Several front-desk staff are mentioned as friendly, helpful, and fluent in English, which matters a lot in a tourist city with as many international guests as Pattaya · Many praise the quick check-in, the help recommending restaurants, booking Koh Larn tours, and arranging cars, which leaves guests feeling they got more service than they paid for · But to be straight, some reviews say the team's responsiveness isn't equally consistent at all times, especially when the hotel is full or a tour group checks in at once · Overall service is still a strong point and one reason the review score holds at the 8.8 level.

What real reviews say (the praise and the gripes) — Pulled together from Trip.com, Booking.com, and TripAdvisor, the picture lines up fairly closely · On the praise side: a Central Pattaya location within walking distance of the beach and Walking Street, next to The Avenue with a 7-Eleven across the street, a rooftop sky pool with city views that kids love, clean and well-kept rooms, comfortable beds, friendly English-speaking staff, a varied breakfast, and value that many reiterate as "for what you pay, this is good" · On the gripes side: the most-mentioned issue is the fairly small room size and lack of a balcony · Next is noise — the walls between rooms and the corridor soundproofing aren't thick enough, and you sometimes hear neighbors or the nightlife district around the hotel at night, a fairly small rooftop pool, and some details starting to show age, given the building has been open since 2014 · These gripes are fixable by choosing your room, asking for a higher floor on the inner side, and setting expectations to match the price, rather than being big problems that keep people from coming back.

"Clean room, comfortable bed, lovely staff who were very helpful. My only gripe is the room is a bit small and there's no balcony. On the Friday night I heard some noise from the corridor — next time I'll ask for a higher floor on the inner side instead."

Price comparison and value — The starting price for a Standard room is around THB 1,000/night on weekdays in the off-season (some promotions dip down to THB 900), rising to roughly THB 1,600–2,000+ over long weekends or in high season · The family Quadruple sits higher than that, according to size and number of guests · Compared with chain hotels of the same level in Central Pattaya, such as Ibis Pattaya or Holiday Inn Express at similar or slightly higher prices, Travelodge feels like excellent value among affordable 3-star hotels, especially once you count in the rooftop sky pool, the location next to The Avenue, the walk to the beach, and the praised service · If you plan to use Central Pattaya as a base for walking to the beach, shopping, and eating and drinking every day, every baht you spend on this location and pool pays off in full · The thing to weigh up is that if you prioritize a spacious room or a sea view, you may need to add to the budget and look at the beachfront resorts instead.

Things to know before booking — A few things help make the stay smoother · One, if you're a light sleeper or sensitive to noise, specify when you book that you want a higher floor on the inner side that doesn't face the road or main corridor, because this area is lively and the soundproofing isn't thick · Two, check clearly whether your booked package includes breakfast, because some rates don't and you pay extra per person · Three, if you're coming as a group or with children, look at the Family Quadruple, which is more spacious and better value than booking two small rooms · Four, during Pattaya's high season (November–February and long weekends) prices rise fast, so book ahead and compare across several platforms · Five, if you're driving yourself, ask about parking in advance, because parking in Central Pattaya is fairly limited · Six, go with free cancellation first if your plans aren't firm yet, because prices tend to change with the season.

The verdict — From all the real reviews, Travelodge Pattaya is the best fit for people who want to stay in the middle of Central Pattaya on an affordable budget, with a no-surprises chain standard · A rooftop sky pool, a location next to The Avenue, a walk to the beach and Walking Street, clean rooms, and friendly service make it good enough value that it's hard to find a rival at the same price · If you're after a spacious room with a balcony, a full sea view, or beachfront-resort quiet, this may not be the answer, and you should consider a resort on the Jomtien or Pratumnak side instead · But for a Pattaya trip where you want a great location, everything within walking distance, a rooftop pool, and a price that's easy on the wallet — Travelodge Pattaya covers almost all of that, and it's why the review score has stayed high year after year.

faq.a: The hotel is on Soi Pattaya 15, Nongprue, Bang Lamung in the Central Pattaya area, right next to The Avenue Pattaya mall · It's about a 1 km walk to Pattaya Beach and Walking Street (12–18 min) · It's near Ripley's Believe It or Not, about 0.4 km away, with a 7-Eleven across the street · CentralFestival is about 2–2.5 km away and U-Tapao Airport is about a 40 min drive

faq.q: What's the starting price at Travelodge Pattaya, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start from around THB 1,000/night for a Standard room on weekdays · There's Standard Plus (King bed), Standard Twin, Standard Queen, and the family Friends & Family Quadruple that sleeps up to 4 · Prices in high season (November–February) and on long weekends rise fast, so compare several platforms before booking

faq.q: Does Travelodge Pattaya have a pool and breakfast?
faq.a: Yes — a rooftop sky pool with a poolside bar and Pattaya city views, plus a 24-hour gym · Breakfast is a Western-Asian buffet at The Lodge (around 6:00 AM–10:30 AM) · One thing to know is that some room packages don't include breakfast and you pay extra per person (children up to 17 usually go free), so check when booking

faq.q: Who is Travelodge Pattaya best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for couples, solo travelers, groups of friends, and small families who want to stay in the middle of Central Pattaya on an affordable budget, walking to the beach, shopping, and the food-and-drink scene every day · It has a sky pool and a chain standard at an affordable price · If you're after a spacious room with a balcony or a resort-style sea view, the Jomtien or Pratumnak side may suit you better

faq.q: What are the noise and room size like at Travelodge Pattaya?
faq.a: Many reviews agree that the rooms are fairly small and have no balcony, and the soundproofing between rooms and the corridor isn't very thick, so you sometimes hear neighbors or the nightlife district around the hotel at night · If you're a light sleeper, we recommend asking for a higher floor or the inner side that doesn't face the road when you book or check in · If you're coming as a group, choose the Family Quadruple, which is more spacious

faq.q: Is Travelodge Pattaya good value compared with other hotels in Central Pattaya?
faq.a: Compared with chains of the same level like ibis Pattaya or Holiday Inn Express at similar or higher prices, Travelodge is excellent value among affordable 3-star hotels, especially once you count in the rooftop sky pool, the location next to The Avenue, the walk to the beach, and the praised service · The thing to weigh up is that if you prioritize a spacious room or a sea view, you may need to add to the budget for a beachfront resort
